verdict: United's revenue jumped 17% to a record $17.9B on strong premium, loyalty and cargo demand, but a 62% surge in fuel costs held net income to $1.0B.

kpis.label: Revenue growth
kpis.note: total operating revenue was a record $17.9B, vs $15.2B a year ago

kpis.label: EPS (GAAP)
kpis.note: diluted, vs $2.90 a year ago; adjusted EPS was $2.54 after removing special credits

kpis.label: Aircraft fuel cost
kpis.note: up 62% YoY — $1.8B more than a year ago, at $3.90 a gallon vs $2.43

kpis.label: Passenger revenue
kpis.note: up 18% YoY; premium-cabin revenue rose 17% and cargo revenue rose 23%

segments.name: Passenger
segments.note: Tickets and seat-related fees — about 91% of revenue. Premium products and loyalty-linked flying led growth; United carried a record 49.5 million passengers in the quarter.

segments.name: Cargo
segments.note: Freight and mail flown in the bellies of passenger planes.

segments.name: Other
segments.note: Loyalty-program revenue from partners such as credit-card issuers, plus maintenance and other services sold to third parties. The statement line is $1,106M; shown as $1,105M so the rounded segments tie to the $17,875M total (see footer).

opex.name: Salaries and related costs
opex.note: Pay and benefits for about 118,000 employees, including $146M of profit sharing — United's largest single cost, up 9% YoY.

opex.name: Depreciation & amortization
opex.note: Spreading the cost of aircraft and equipment over their working lives.

opex.name: Distribution expenses
opex.note: The cost of selling tickets — booking channels, card fees and commissions.

opex.name: Other operating expenses, net
opex.note: All remaining operating costs ($2,739M on the statement), reduced by $215M of special credits — mainly gains on aircraft sale-leaseback deals — and $1M of rounding so the flow ties (see footer).

otherDetail: Interest expense of $359M, partly offset by $157M of interest income, $56M of capitalized interest and $24M of miscellaneous income, less a $13M unrealized loss on investments — a net $135M cost below operating income.
follow100Note: Cost of revenue groups the direct costs of flying: aircraft fuel ($4,843M), landing fees and other rent ($1,046M), aircraft maintenance materials and outside repairs ($806M) and regional capacity purchase — paying regional airlines to fly United Express routes ($725M). Every other operating expense line sits in operating expenses, so each statement line is counted exactly once.

takeaways.title: A record quarter for demand
takeaways.text: Revenue rose 17% to a record $17,875M. Premium revenue rose 17%, loyalty revenue 17%, cargo 23% and contracted business revenue 26% — and United expects even faster growth, over 20%, in the December quarter.

takeaways.title: Fuel ate most of the growth
takeaways.text: Aircraft fuel cost $4,843M, up $1,846M from a year ago, as the average price rose to $3.90 a gallon from $2.43. Operating income rose only 4% to $1,446M despite the record top line.

takeaways.title: Adjusted profit strips out sale gains
takeaways.text: GAAP EPS was $3.14, but that includes $215M of special credits, mostly gains from selling aircraft and leasing them back. Excluding those and a $13M investment loss, adjusted EPS was $2.54 and adjusted net income was $833M.

oneTimers: Operating results include $215M of net special credits: $213M of net gains on sale of assets and other special charges — primarily $294M of gains on aircraft sale-leaseback transactions, partly offset by other charges — which is why GAAP EPS of $3.14 sits above adjusted EPS of $2.54.
footerNote: Flow adaptation: airlines report no gross-profit line; cost of revenue here groups the direct costs of flying (see the $100 note). United's release is in $M and its own lines carry $1M of rounding — the revenue lines sum to $17,876M against a $17,875M total, and the expense lines to $16,430M against $16,429M — so two 'other' lines are each shown $1M lower here so the rounded flow ties exactly to the reported totals.
